lead.headline: Safety claims need independent proof
lead.summary: A newly released US audit and a UK parliamentary report make the case for independent testing. A US vehicle inquiry and an English and Welsh police-user survey show why oversight must be tested where systems are used.

stories.title: Independent tests exposed historical safeguards gaps
stories.summary: US GAO tested four selected AI platforms in spring 2026 and found that each could yield harmful assistance under its assigned scenario. The agency released its audit publicly on 18 November. These observations do not establish a present-day failure rate, rank the platforms or document actual harm. Recheck safeguards after significant model updates.

stories.title: A parliamentary recommendation is not a safeguard in force
stories.summary: On 18 November, a UK House of Commons committee recommended stronger frontier-AI oversight, including an independent regulator. Its report is advice to government, not enacted law. Track the government response, the powers eventually proposed and the evidence of their use.

stories.title: Human review needs a comprehension check
stories.summary: A Home Office survey of facial-search users in England and Wales obtained 779 valid voluntary responses. The respondent findings cannot describe the whole population or the accuracy of the algorithm. Audit comprehension, how a suggested match is corroborated, and how a person can correct an error.

stories.title: A deployed fix is not a verified outcome
stories.summary: In a 6 November filing, NHTSA opened a recall query into the effectiveness of a previous Waymo school-bus remedy. This is a continuing watchpoint, not a new incident, final causation finding or exposure-adjusted estimate. Ask for version-specific tests and evidence of the corrected behaviour.

stories.title: Australia can ask for evidence before deployment
stories.summary: Australia’s 10 November policy announcement outlined proposed AI safety and security protections. That is not evidence of enacted protections or an effective remedy. A practical step now is to require a named decision-maker and to test the route for stopping, reversing or contesting a consequential decision.

threat.disclaimer: No current tier assigned. Target six labels are approved, numeric boundaries unverified. Preserve five-tier public display until renderer, archive and mobile compatibility tests pass. SIX-TIER DISPLAY PENDING VERIFICATION.

outlook.label: Require a versioned record of human control
outlook.summary: For an important deployment, record the system version, the person authorised to intervene, the observed result of their intervention and the correction or appeal route. Then retest after material changes.

report.title: What counts as proof that a safeguard works?
report.standfirst: The evidence is strongest when an independent reviewer can test a particular safeguard and identify what it did not prove.
report.intro: This edition separates the two newly published findings from continuing watchpoints. The evidence does not support aggregate safety scores, a platform ranking or a global trend.

incidents.name: Waymo school-bus passing reports / recall-remedy query
incidents.date: Recall remedy 17 Nov 2025; inquiry opened 6 Nov 2026
incidents.classification: Confirmed open regulator inquiry; causes unresolved
incidents.known: The inquiry covers 2,895 fifth-generation ADS vehicles and investigates post-remedy reports; final cause is not established.
incidents.unknown: Number of all incidents, causal mechanism, exposure denominators, injury outcomes and effective updated remedy.
incidents.lesson: A deployed fix is not independent evidence that the hazard has stopped in representative conditions.

investigativeSummary: A controlled audit, a parliamentary recommendation, an open regulator inquiry and a volunteer survey answer different questions. We do not combine them into a safety score or infer that a policy proposal or installed fix is already effective. The common practical test is whether people can understand, stop and contest a consequential decision.
